title: Quantum Memory Advantage from Contextuality
summary: Quantum contextuality is a vital non-classical resource, yet illuminating the precise mechanisms through which it enables unconditional computational advantages remains a challenge. We translate graph-theoretic formulations of contextuality into an unconditional quantum memory advantage for formal language recognition. We define a promise problem on an exclusivity graph $G$ where any classical finite automaton respecting exclusivity requires $N \ge χ(G)$ memory states, whereas a QFA requires a memory of dimension $d = ξ(G)$.
